historical.text: Coastal strip around Kalyan, traditionally taken from Adil Shahi control in 1657. Its borders here are simplified.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Core region of Shivaji's early rule. By 1659 it is generally described as under his administration, though subject to outside pressure; its status here is simplified.
Hill country around Purandar fort. Maratha possession since about 1648 is traditional; details of how it came about are disputed.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Mountain district around Raigad fort, described as Shivaji's principal seat from the mid-1650s. His later coronation there (1674) falls outside this scenario.
sources: Mehendale, Gajanan B. Shivaji: His Life and Times

historical.text: Forested hill region around Mahabaleshwar, traditionally taken from the More family in 1656, with Pratapgad built nearby soon afterwards.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: District in the Krishna valley under Adil Shahi administration. Afzal Khan is traditionally linked with this area at the start of the 1659 expedition, though accounts of his base differ.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Abstract region standing for the upland routes between Wai and the south. Its exact boundaries are a gameplay simplification.
Hill country around Panhala fort near Kolhapur. Traditional accounts say Shivaji took it in late 1659 and that it was besieged in 1660.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

historical.text: Coastal strip south of the Raigad area, contested between Adil Shahi holdings and Maratha raids around 1659-60. Details are uncertain.
Capital region of the Adil Shahi Sultanate. An abstract off-map heartland: distances are not to scale.
sources: Eaton, Richard M. A Social History of the Deccan, 1300-1761 (Cambridge, 2005)
